title: Make changes with confidence
summary: Plan the change and the way back.

passages.heading: The core idea
passages.markdown: A change request explains what will change, why it is needed, which systems are affected, and who is responsible. Assess the risk, dependencies, expected disruption, and acceptance criteria before scheduling work. A maintenance window sets a planned time for implementation, while a change freeze restricts changes during a sensitive period. Follow the organization’s approval path; an urgent request still needs the appropriate emergency process rather than an undocumented shortcut.

passages.heading: In the real world
passages.markdown: Test the proposed change in a suitable environment and prepare both a backup plan and a rollback plan. A backup preserves recoverable data, while a rollback plan defines the steps and conditions for returning to a previous state. Decide in advance when to stop an unsuccessful implementation so the recovery window remains usable. During execution, record actions and results, communicate status to affected people, and verify the agreed acceptance criteria. Close the change only after the required review and user acceptance, recording lessons that will make the next change safer.

passages.heading: Make it stick
passages.markdown: Put it into practice by explaining the decision in your own words. In a support scenario, identify the requirement first, connect it to the relevant technology, and check the result against that requirement. If the evidence changes, revisit your reasoning rather than repeating the same action. Document what you observed so the next person can understand your conclusion.
